newsitem.title: UK: Russia, China key to boosting world sugar prices.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China key to boosting world sugar prices.

text.p: Russian and Chinese sugar demand will be pivotal for any world price recovery before spring 1997 but the overhanging surplus will still be a bearish element, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Monday. "It would appear that without Russian and Chinese purchases it would be difficult to reverse the existing mid-term bearish trend, at least until spring 1997," the ISO said in its latest November market report.
This would be when new crop outputs and the intentions of southern hemisphere exporters became clear, it said.
The ISO said there was little room for Russia to import sugar and forecast Russia's net import requirements at nearly three million tonnes for 1996/97.
"It does not look unlikely that Russia will enter the world market before the end of winter 1997," it said.

Despite its poor beet crop, the Russian domestic market -- well protected by duties -- was flush with supply of whites from both its own production and that of neighbouring Ukraine at prices as low as $400 a tonne.
This equated to around $260 in the port of destination or at the border before import duties, value-added tax and handling costs were added, it said.

The ISO estimated China's net import demand at 1.48 million tonnes, raw value, for next year and noted that industry sources did not expect imports until after June when the Chinese requirement could be between 1.5 and 2.0 million tonnes. "In the case of China, it has always been notoriously difficult to predict the buying intentions of Beijing," it said.
